label: MongoDB
description: Tools to query and explore a MongoDB database

tools.name: AggregateDocuments
tools.description:
Execute a MongoDB aggregation pipeline on a collection.

ONLY use this tool if you have already loaded the schema of the collection you need to query.
Load the collection's schema first if it is not already known.

Returns a list of JSON strings, where each string represents a
result document from the aggregation
(tools cannot return complex types).

Aggregation pipelines allow for complex data processing including:
* $match - filter documents
* $group - group documents and perform calculations
* $project - reshape documents
* $sort - sort documents
* $limit - limit results
* $lookup - join with other collections
* And many more stages

parameters.name: pipeline
parameters.description: MongoDB aggregation pipeline as a list of JSON strings, each representing a stage. Example: ['{"$match": {"status": "active"}}', '{"$group": {"_id": "$category", "count": {"$sum": 1}}}']

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of results to return from the aggregation. Defaults to 1000.

tools.name: CountDocuments
tools.description: Count documents in a MongoDB collection matching the given filter.

parameters.name: filter_dict
parameters.description: MongoDB filter/query as JSON string. Example: '{"status": "active"}'. Defaults to no filter, which counts all documents.

tools.name: ListCollections
tools.description:
Discover all the collections in the MongoDB database.

Use when the list of collections is not known.
ALWAYS use this tool before any other tool that requires a collection name.

parameters.name: database_name
parameters.description: The database name to discover collections in

tools.name: ListDatabases
tools.description: Discover all the databases in the MongoDB instance.

output.description: The databases in the MongoDB instance

tools.name: ListFields
tools.description:
Get the schema/structure of a MongoDB collection by sampling documents.

Since MongoDB is schema-less, this tool samples a configurable number of documents
to infer the schema structure and data types.

This tool should ALWAYS be used before executing any query.
All collections in the query must be discovered first by listing the database's collections.

parameters.name: database_name
parameters.description: The database name to get the collection schema of

parameters.name: collection_name
parameters.description: The collection to get the schema of

parameters.name: sample_size
parameters.description: The number of documents to sample for schema discovery. Defaults to 1000.

tools.name: QueryDocuments
tools.description:
Find documents in a MongoDB collection.

ONLY use this tool if you have already loaded the schema of the collection you need to query.
Load the collection's schema first if it is not already known.

Returns a list of JSON strings, where each string represents a
document from the collection (tools cannot return complex types).

When running queries, follow these rules which will help avoid errors:
* Always specify projection to limit fields returned if you don't need all data.
* Always sort your results by the most relevant fields first. Use '_id' if you're unsure.
* Use appropriate MongoDB query operators for complex filtering ($gte, $lte, $in, $regex, etc.).
* Be mindful of case sensitivity when querying string fields.
* Use indexes when possible (typically on _id and commonly queried fields).

parameters.name: filter_dict
parameters.description: MongoDB filter/query as JSON string. Example: '{"status": "active", "age": {"$gte": 18}}'. Defaults to no filter, which finds all documents.

parameters.name: projection
parameters.description: Fields to include/exclude as JSON string. Use 1 to include, 0 to exclude. Example: '{"name": 1, "email": 1, "_id": 0}'. Defaults to all fields.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort criteria as list of JSON strings, each containing 'field' and 'direction' keys. Use 1 for ascending, -1 for descending. Example: ['{"field": "name", "direction": 1}', '{"field": "created_at", "direction": -1}']. Defaults to no sort.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of documents to return. Defaults to 1000.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: The number of documents to skip. Defaults to 0.

summary:
## MongoDB Toolkit

Provides tools for querying and exploring a MongoDB database from Arcade agents. Enables schema discovery, document retrieval, aggregation pipelines, and collection/database enumeration.

## Capabilities

- **Schema & structure discovery**: List all databases, enumerate collections within a database, and sample documents to infer field names and data types for schema-less collections.
- **Document querying**: Find documents with filtering, projection, sorting, and MongoDB query operators (`$gte`, `$in`, `$regex`, etc.).
- **Aggregation pipelines**: Execute multi-stage pipelines (`$match`, `$group`, `$project`, `$sort`, `$lookup`, and more) for complex data processing and cross-collection joins.
- **Document counting**: Count documents matching an arbitrary filter without fetching full documents.

## Secrets

`MONGODB_CONNECTION_STRING` — The full MongoDB connection URI used to authenticate and connect to the MongoDB instance. This string encodes the protocol, credentials (username and password), host(s), port, and database name, for example: `mongodb+srv://user:password@cluster.example.mongodb.net/mydb`. Obtain it from your MongoDB provider:

- **MongoDB Atlas**: Navigate to your cluster in the [Atlas dashboard](https://cloud.mongodb.com), click **Connect**, choose **Drivers**, and copy the connection string. Replace the `<password>` placeholder with the actual database user password. The user must have at least read permissions on the target database (or read/write if mutations are needed). Create database users under **Database Access** in the Atlas UI.
- **Self-hosted MongoDB**: Construct the URI manually using the host, port, and credentials configured in your `mongod` instance or `mongos` router. Refer to the [MongoDB connection string documentation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/connection-string/) for syntax details.

For storing secrets in Arcade, see the [Arcade secrets guide](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/guides/create-tools/tool-basics/create-tool-secrets) and manage them at [https://api.arcade.dev/dashboard/auth/secrets](https://api.arcade.dev/dashboard/auth/secrets).
